classification.difficultyReason: Establishes identities and inequalities for arbitrary real inputs by comparing symbolic function values.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Let $f(x)=2x$. Show that $f(a+b)=f(a)+f(b)$ and $f(ka)=kf(a)$ for all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $k$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(a+b)&=2(a+b)\\f(a+b)&=2a+2b\\f(a+b)&=f(a)+f(b).\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}f(ka)&=2ka\\f(ka)&=k(2a)\\f(ka)&=kf(a).\end{align*}$$
Both identities hold for all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $k$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Let $f(x)=x+2$. Show that $f(a+b)\ne f(a)+f(b)$ for any real numbers $a$ and $b$. Also show that $f(ka)\ne kf(a)$ for all real numbers $a$ and $k$ unless $k=1$.

answer.short: $f(a+b)=a+b+2$, whereas $f(a)+f(b)=a+b+4$, so they are unequal. Also, $f(ka)=ka+2$ and $kf(a)=ka+2k$ are equal only when $k=1$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(a+b)&=a+b+2,\\f(a)+f(b)&=(a+2)+(b+2)\\f(a)+f(b)&=a+b+4.\end{align*}$$
The two values differ by $2$, so $f(a+b)\ne f(a)+f(b)$ for every real $a$ and $b$.
$$\begin{align*}f(ka)&=ka+2,\\kf(a)&=k(a+2)\\kf(a)&=ka+2k.\end{align*}$$
Equality requires
$$\begin{align*}ka+2&=ka+2k\\2&=2k\\k&=1.\end{align*}$$
When $k=1$, both expressions equal $a+2$. Hence $f(ka)\ne kf(a)$ whenever $k\ne1$.
